original_question: Is every contact Fano manifold homogeneous?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Conjecture 7: "A contact Fano manifold is homogeneous," stated explicitly as a rephrasing of Conjecture 6. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended target almost exactly: it has the correct universal quantifier ("every"), the correct class of objects (contact Fano manifolds), and the correct property under question (homogeneity). In Beauville's paper this is precisely Conjecture 7. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
missing_details: It should specify the geometric setting: the paper is working over the complex numbers, with X a complex projective manifold. Beauville opens the section with "Let X be a complex manifold" and frames the classification problem for projective contact manifolds. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, it should unpack "contact" as a holomorphic contact structure on an odd-dimensional manifold X of dimension 2r+1, given by a twisted 1-form θ with values in a line bundle L such that θ∧(dθ)^r is nowhere zero. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

It should make the Fano hypothesis explicit as the ampleness of -K_X; Beauville notes in the definition paragraph that the contact condition implies K_X = L^-(r+1). ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

It should clarify the intended meaning of "homogeneous" in this context by pointing to the paper's type (b) models: the adjoint varieties X_g attached to simple complex Lie algebras. Beauville says a homogeneous Fano contact manifold is of type (b). ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

If one wants the question to be completely self-contained, one should mention that type (b) means: for a simple complex Lie algebra g, X_g is the unique closed orbit of the adjoint group in P(g), and X_g is a contact Fano manifold. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

There are no ambient-ring, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic "for sufficiently large m" issues in this problem; the missing information is geometric context and the precise definition of a holomorphic contact structure. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a complex projective manifold of odd dimension 2r+1 endowed with a holomorphic contact structure, i.e. a twisted 1-form θ∈H^0(X,Ω_X^1⊗L) for some line bundle L such that θ∧(dθ)^r is nowhere zero, and assume that X is Fano. Must X be homogeneous? ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation from Section 4: is every projective contact manifold either (a) the projective cotangent bundle P(T^*M) of a compact complex manifold M, or (b) the adjoint variety X_g, namely the unique closed orbit of the adjoint group of a simple complex Lie algebra g in P(g)? Beauville explicitly says Conjecture 7 is a rephrasing of this Conjecture 6. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the right statement and should not be broadened: Beauville formulates the exact question as Conjecture 7 in Section 4. The nearby context that makes it stand-alone is the section-opening definition of a holomorphic contact structure, together with the immediately preceding classification setup listing the two known types of compact holomorphic contact manifolds. The only alternate formulation worth giving is Conjecture 6, because the paper itself explicitly says that Conjecture 7 is just a rephrasing of it after recalling the known reduction to the Fano case. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
